transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for coming in today. I wanted to sit down with you and talk about the developmental screening for your grandson.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, thank you doctor. I have been praying on this, just hoping everything is moving along as it should for the little one.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have something to tell you that is difficult. There was a mistake in how we handled the referral for that screening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When the first appointment was declined, someone in our office marked the referral as completed in the computer system. Because of that, we didn't follow up to schedule a new date, and the screening hasn't actually happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I trusted the process. I truly believed we were in good hands, that this was part of a plan for him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is upsetting to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's more than upsetting. It feels like he's just a number to you people. My heart is just sinking thinking about the time we've lost.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this caused. We've been very overwhelmed in the clinic lately, and the system just didn't flag it for us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does the system matter? I am talking about my grandson's life. I just feel so alone in this, like I'm the only one who cares about his future.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling let down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I am. I feel very let down. Do you actually understand what this means for a child's growth?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do. I want to make sure I've explained it clearly enough. Do you understand why the appointment didn't happen?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand that someone clicked a button they shouldn't have and now my grandson is behind.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it too late? Tell me the truth. Did we miss the window?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we haven't missed the window for the screening itself. But we do need to act now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I feel like we are being tested. I pray every day for his health, and then I come here and find out the doctors aren't paying attention.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just so cold. This whole place feels so cold.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I want to make this right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? How do you fix a mistake that's already happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to personally call the screening center this afternoon. I will find the next available opening, even if it's a cancellation, and I will call you by tomorrow at noon to give you the exact date and time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what do I need to do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just need you to keep your phone nearby tomorrow. Once I give you the date, I'll need you to confirm that the time works for your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that. But I just don't know if I can trust the office again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that trust is broken. I'm the one responsible for making sure this gets finished now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will pray that you actually do it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will get that call made today.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to express distress without interruption and remains regulated throughout the pushback.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('explained it clearly enough' and 'Do you understand why').

A.justification: Apology is offered but diluted by an excuse regarding being 'overwhelmed in the clinic' and the system not flagging the error.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('feeling let down') and engages emotional bids, though only one specific emotion is named.

T.justification: Specific next steps and timelines are provided (call today, update by tomorrow noon) and the patient's role is defined, but prevention is not addressed.
